clue.text: Maybe Derby County's beginning to go after Division One

indicators.note: the county's first letter is placed after the division in the answer

parts.note: a first division is CLASS I, class one

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word County is used

explanation.surface: A football fan muses on Derby County returning to the top division.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about Derby County football club; here Derby is the horse race, one of Britain's five flat-racing Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby at Epsom is one of the five English horse races known collectively as the Classics, so it is an example.

clue.text: Anxieties leading to second stroke

parts.note: worries or anxieties are cares

explanation.surface: Worries build up until a second stroke follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke someone gently is to fondle them affectionately; both words are verbs of tender touching.

clue.text: First two characters on trail reported missing

parts.note: the first two letters of the alphabet are A and B

indicators.note: the word for a trail is said out loud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by a hound

explanation.surface: Two people first seen on a trail are now said to be missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' makes the trail word a sound-alike: SCENT is heard as SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing from class is away, not present, which is the synonym needed.

clue.text: A Martian's vaporised American exploratory craft

indicators.note: something vaporised is blasted apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A science-fiction Martian zaps an American space probe into vapour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern space probe; the craft is Columbus's flagship of 1492. 'vaporised' scatters A MARTIANS into SANTAMARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbus sailed his flagship of that name on the 1492 voyage that reached the Americas, a vessel of discovery.

clue.text: Fruit tree, an energy source briefly retaining oxygen

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: carb is the short form of carbohydrate, a source of energy in food
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A tree whose fruit gives quick energy and takes in oxygen, as plants do.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean locust bean tree bears edible pods used as a chocolate substitute, so it is a fruit tree.

clue.text: Person immobilising van occupied by learner

indicators.note: the van has the learner sitting inside it

parts.note: a camper is a camper van
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A parking enforcer wheel-locks a camper van with a learner driver inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A clamper fits a wheel clamp to an illegally parked car, a familiar British parking penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel-clamp operator stops a parked car from moving, immobilising it until a fine is paid.

clue.text: Newspaper's against plugging replica enamelwork

indicators.note: these pieces are pushed into a gap in the other, like a plug

parts.note: a clone is an exact copy or replica
the i is a British newspaper, plus the S of the possessive
leaning against a wall is leaning on it

explanation.surface: A newspaper campaigns against advertising fake enamel ware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' looks like promoting, but it is the insertion signal: ISON goes inside CLONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a decorative technique where coloured enamel fills compartments formed by metal wires, a kind of enamel art.

clue.text: Records omitting Brunel's section of bridge, perhaps

indicators.note: this part is left out of the longer word

parts.note: an archive is a collection of records
Brunel is the setter, so 'Brunel has' is I'VE

explanation.surface: Records of the engineer Brunel lack details of one of his bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: Brunel is the setter's pseudonym, borrowed from the Victorian bridge builder Isambard Kingdom Brunel; the setter speaking of himself gives I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Many bridges are built from curved spans, so one span is an example of a bridge component, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Idiots cut up about senior teacher

indicators.note: the reversed cut goes around the teacher
in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to snip is to cut
the head is the senior teacher of a school

explanation.surface: Idiots get angry about the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' reads as upset, but 'up' turns the word for cut round to PINS, and 'about' wraps that round the senior teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a pin-sized brain is an insult for a stupid person, a colloquial synonym for fools.

clue.text: These improve vehicle safety, except in luxury car

indicators.note: the word for except goes inside the car

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce, a luxury car
bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Safety features fitted to all cars except a luxury model.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong roof bars that protect occupants if a car overturns are fitted to make vehicles safer.

clue.text: Check trousers stained at front with sticky substance

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket or take in

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: only the first letter of stained is used

explanation.surface: Someone checks their trousers, stained at the front with something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, so REIN takes S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree sap that hardens into a gummy material is a classic sticky substance.

clue.text: Act on oral treatment for tooth cavity?

indicators.note: treating the letters means working them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dentist acts with oral treatment on a decayed tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' reads as dental care but is the anagram signal on ACT ON ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The channel in a tooth root holding the pulp is a hollow space inside the tooth, also the name of the procedure.

clue.text: Smart outfit? Yes, but smeared with sand

indicators.note: smearing messes things up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's smart clothes are fine, except for being smeared with beach sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the finest clothes kept for church and special occasions, a smart outfit.

clue.text: Father Brown entertains sage, possibly

indicators.note: the two words together hold the answer inside them, as a host holds guests

explanation.surface: G. K. Chesterton's priest-detective Father Brown hosts a wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like a wise man for Father Brown to entertain; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a culinary plant used for flavouring, an example of the category, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Coach one boards after pursuit

parts.note: post- is the prefix meaning after

indicators.note: boarding a vehicle means getting inside it

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone climbs aboard a coach after a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed horse-drawn carriage hired for travelling by stages was a kind of coach.

clue.text: In sequence

parts.note: the sequence in which cricketers go in to bat

explanation.surface: Things arranged in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batters 'go in' to bat one after another; the order they go in is this sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The list setting when each cricketer goes in to bat is a sequence of 'ins'.

clue.text: Strangely, Trump (no politician) has use for this intellectual tome

indicators.note: strangely arranged letters come out in an odd new order
here no means without, so the politician is taken out of the name

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Odd that Donald Trump, supposedly no politician, would ever use a highbrow book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes MP from TRUMP leaving TRU; then 'Strangely' mixes TRU, HAS and USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is a weighty word-reference work, the kind of tome a word lover uses.

clue.text: President to want Republican backing in East Coast city

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: in a down clue the words go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to need is to want

explanation.surface: A US president wants Republican support in an East Coast city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the American East Coast; the city is Aberdeen on Scotland's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The granite city in north-east Scotland lies on the North Sea, an east-coast city.

clue.text: Blast Noel and Pam's unnecessary words

indicators.note: blasting things scatters them, so these letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone curses Noel and Pam for their pointless chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an exclamation but signals the anagram of NOEL and PAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: This term for redundancy names using more words than needed, like 'free gift'; the clue gives the words themselves.

clue.text: Combatants reeling dazedly, overwhelmed by blows

indicators.note: the word being swamped sits inside the word for blows

parts.note: belts are hard punches or blows

indicators.note: something dazed is confused, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Fighters reel in a daze, beaten down by punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dazedly' scrambles the clue's reeling into LIGEREN, and 'overwhelmed by' tucks that inside the word for blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations or parties waging war are fighters, the people engaged in combat.

clue.text: Welsh girl had new guy round a lot

indicators.note: turned round, the letters read in the opposite direction
most of these words is used: the h of had and the uy of guy are dropped

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl had a new boyfriend over very often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' takes most of the letters of 'had new guy', ADNEWG, and 'round' turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female forename of Welsh origin, so it names a Welsh girl.

clue.text: Set rate paid, inclusive of grain

indicators.note: the abbreviation has the grain included within it

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid on a bill
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A fee is settled, with the grain thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods given a fixed cost have had a figure put on them, so the verb means having a rate fixed.

clue.text: Drive around? No time or opportunity

indicators.note: no means without here, so the letter is removed
turned around, the word reads backwards

parts.note: to motor is to drive

explanation.surface: No time or chance to drive around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses MOTOR to ROTOM, and 'No time' removes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Having leeway or scope to do something, as in 'room for improvement', is having the opportunity.

clue.text: Does she demonstrate pet project in stateside gift-giving bash

definitions.meaning: one's pet project is one's baby, and a person who shows it off would be its shower
an American party where guests bring presents for a mother-to-be

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's second word as 'one who shows', not a rain shower or bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The party is held in the US for an expectant mother, with friends giving gifts for the newborn.

clue.text: Sound made in Alps, intermittently, by loud bell

indicators.note: only every other letter of the phrase is taken, with gaps between

explanation.surface: A cowbell clangs loudly now and then in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling song of Alpine herdsmen switches between chest voice and falsetto, a traditional mountain call.

clue.text: Picked up gardening tools and sprinkler

indicators.note: picking up a sound means hearing it, so the tools' word is taken as heard

parts.note: hoes are gardening tools for weeding

explanation.surface: A gardener picks up tools and the sprinkler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like lifting tools, but signals the sound-alike: HOES is heard as HOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible watering pipe sprays water over a garden, so it serves as a sprinkler.

clue.text: In love, shown by distracted demeanour

indicators.note: a distracted mind is scattered, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone's dreamy, distracted manner shows they are smitten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be captivated or besotted with someone is to be smitten, in love.

clue.text: It's charged by leaders of imperial cavalry and foot

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Imperial cavalry and infantry are led into a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like infantry beside the cavalry, but it is the definition: a metrical foot in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody this is a metrical foot of four syllables, two long and two short.

clue.text: More than one song book

definitions.meaning: songs in a show are ..., so several tunes
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece is a 'number', so several are this; it is also the Bible book after Leviticus.

clue.text: Lure fish over to side away from wind

indicators.note: turned over, the combined word reads backwards

parts.note: to draw someone is to lure them
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler lures a fish over to the sheltered side.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, this is the side sheltered from the wind, facing away from where it blows.
